description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994).  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00.

REPRODUCER: `use FileHandle; print "ok\n";` and `use IPC::Cmd;`  perl: loads    PCL: dies at FileHandle.pm line 60 (`my $c = *{"${pkg}::$func"}{CODE} or die "${pkg}::$func missing";` over IO::Handle / IO::Seekable / IO::File method lists -- READ the three lists there: every name in them must exist as a CODE slot or FileHandle cannot load).
perl's IO::Seekable: `getpos` answers an opaque position (in practice `tell`), `setpos($pos)` = `seek($pos, 0)`; both are XS in perl (IO.xs) over fgetpos/fsetpos.  In PCL they are two one-line methods over the runtime's tell/seek in whatever owns IO::Seekable today (lib/IO/Handle.pm is the only IO shim in lib/ -- find where IO::Seekable / IO::File come from: the real .pm files transpiled, or the runtime).  Probe the OTHER names in FileHandle.pm's three lists the same way (`perl -e` loop over the lists calling `defined &{"${pkg}::$func"}` under ./runpcl) and fix every missing one that is a one-liner; file the rest.
Then: `use FileHandle; my $fh = FileHandle->new("< $0"); print scalar <$fh>; $fh->close;` and `STDOUT->autoflush(1)` via FileHandle == perl; `use IPC::Cmd qw(can_run run); can_run("ls"); run(command => "echo hi", verbose => 0)` == perl (scalar and list returns).  File what IPC::Cmd still misses, per cause.
BAR: `lib/` or `cl/` change => full sweep + companion io/ legs that use getpos/FileHandle (`grep -a -l`), guard rows in an existing io Pl/t file.


=== DONE (s492c, 2026-09-21, Opus) ===
`IO::Seekable::getpos`/`setpos` and `IO::File::new_tmpfile` are the three
names core FileHandle.pm imports BY GLOB at load and dies on; all three are XS
in perl (IO.xs's fgetpos/fsetpos, tmpfile(3)), so they went into `lib/IO.pm`,
which is already "the XS half of IO, in plain Perl" (#197).

perl's position token is documented as opaque and useful only to setpos, so
getpos/setpos are `tell` and `seek(..., SEEK_SET)`; new_tmpfile is a temp file
opened and then UNLINKED while the handle is open, which is what tmpfile(3)
does on Unix.

`use FileHandle;` now loads, and FileHandle->new / getpos / setpos / autoflush
/ new_tmpfile are identical to perl (probe fh1.pl).  Guard: two rows in
Pl/t/io-shim-01.t (20 -> 22), inverse-verified.

IPC::Cmd still does NOT load -- it reaches Module::Metadata, which hits a
Parser2 capture refusal.  Filed #2058.


=== DONE (s492c) ===
SHIPPED s492c member 6 (8b8e4e93).  IO::Seekable::getpos/setpos and
IO::File::new_tmpfile are XS in perl, so they belong in lib/IO.pm -- already
"the XS half of IO, in plain Perl".  `use FileHandle;` loads again.  Guard: two
rows in Pl/t/io-shim-01.t.  IPC::Cmd still does not load: it pulls
Module::Metadata, which hits a Parser2 refusal -- filed #2058.
subject: EVERYDAY-adjacent (IPC::Cmd, FileHandle): `use FileHandle;` DIES "IO::Seekable::getpos missing at .../FileHandle.pm line 60" -- core FileHandle.pm imports `seek tell getpos setpos` from IO::Seekable by glob at load, and PCL's IO layer has no `getpos`/`setpos`; IPC::Cmd (and anything else that loads FileHandle) falls with it
